component.name: Sonorant
component.summary: Watch what you are listening to

description.p: Sonorant draws what the computer is playing: a scrolling spectrogram of both channels, the spectrum beside it, and broadcast loudness, true peak, dynamic range, tempo and brightness underneath. It follows whatever player is running rather than living inside one, and it can listen to the whole system or to a single app.
The picture is drawn on the GPU at the display's refresh rate while the spectrogram scrolls by audio time, so it moves at the same speed on a 60 Hz panel as on a 240 Hz one.

ul.li: A spectrogram on a note, log or linear frequency axis, in seven palettes
Peak, average and minimum spectra, as a line, bars or LED segments
LUFS momentary, short-term and integrated, loudness range, true peak, crest and overs, to BS.1770
A goniometer, correlation and balance, and waveform lanes
A 3D waterfall you can orbit, and a long history you can zoom and walk back through
A phosphor scope and a beat-reactive backdrop for when it is left running
The title, artwork and transport of whatever is playing, over MPRIS

description.p: Point at the picture to read the frequency under the pointer as hertz and as a note with its deviation in cents, each channel's level there, and how far back in time the column is. Double-click a column to send the player to that moment.

screenshot.caption: Both channels scrolling, with the spectrum beside each pane
Immersive mode, with the panes mirrored and the chrome faded away
The last few seconds as a landscape you can orbit

description.p: The first release built for both systems: everything the Nostalgia+ plugin drew, outside MusicBee and on the GPU, plus the phosphor scope, the zoomable long history, the 3D waterfall and the beat-reactive backdrop.

Since the Windows preview: the picture is held back to line up with what you hear, the frame rate drops while nothing is playing, the OpenGL fallback and software rendering both work, and the right-click menu stays open while it is used, with help rebuilt as a sheet of the settings.
A first Windows preview, before the app was packaged for anything.
